children: Clinically meaningful improvement in disease activity among 8 of 9 evaluable patients, including rapid and marked reductions in proteinuria with complete renal responses
Deep and sustained reduction in pathogenic autoantibodies and IgG reduction underscore potential in plasma-cell driven diseases
Favorable safety profile in patients with refractory SLE

, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company accelerating potential first- or best-in-class, disease-modifying T cell engagers in autoimmune diseases and cancer, today announced clinical data from the ongoing Genrix Bio Phase 1b/2a study of velinotamig (GR1803) in patients with active, refractory, moderate-to-severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The results will be

at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026 on November 8 in Poster #0272, “Initial Results of Velinotamig (GR1803, BCMAxCD3 TCE) Therapy in Patients with Refractory Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: a Phase 1b/2a Study.”

As of the September 8, 2026 data cutoff, 12 patients had been treated across three multi-dose cohorts. Velinotamig demonstrated a favorable safety profile, with no dose-limiting toxicities, no immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity (ICANS), and no Grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome (CRS). CRS occurred in two patients and was limited to Grade 1 or 2 events that resolved with standard management. No Grade 2 events were observed after modifications to the step-up dosing regimen.

Among the first nine patients with at least four weeks of follow-up, clinical activity was observed across measures of disease activity, serologic markers, and renal function. Eight of nine evaluable patients achieved a clinically meaningful reduction of at least four points in SLEDAI-2K. Among seven evaluable patients with urine protein excretion greater than 500 mg/24 hours at baseline, five experienced rapid and marked reductions in proteinuria, and four of these patients achieved a complete renal response as demonstrated by proteinuria levels below 500 mg/24 hours, within 24 weeks. Reductions in anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies and blood IgG, improvement in complement C3, and depletion of CD19-positive B cells were also observed.

“These compelling early findings demonstrate consistent and meaningful clinical, serological, and pharmacodynamic evidence in most treated patients, further validating the therapeutic potential of velinotamig as a short-duration BCMA-directed therapy,” said Jeffrey Jones, MD, MBA, Chief Medical Officer of Cullinan Therapeutics. “Combined with the favorable safety profile observed to date, these data reinforce our confidence in the global development plan for velinotamig, including our initial focus on autoimmune cytopenias, where pathogenic autoantibody-producing plasma cells play a central role in disease pathogenesis. Our unique and complementary clinical stage BCMA- and CD19-directed T cell engager portfolio positions us to address the diverse biology of autoimmune diseases, with the goal of bringing differentiated and tailored treatment options to more patients across a broad range of conditions.”
About the Genrix Bio Phase 1b/2a Velinotamig Study

The open-label, multicenter, dose-escalation Phase 1b/2a study (NCT07348055) is evaluating the safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary efficacy of velinotamig in patients with active, refractory, moderate-to-severe SLE despite at least three months of standard-of-care therapy. Patients receive four intravenous doses on Days 1, 4, 8, and 29, with follow-up for up to 48 weeks. Key assessments include adverse events, CRS, ICANS, DLTs, SLEDAI-2K, 24-hour proteinuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate, anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies, complement C3/C4, and B cell depletion.

Velinotamig is a BCMAxCD3 T cell engager designed to redirect cytotoxic T cells to target BCMA-expressing cells, including pathogenic, autoantibody-producing plasma cells. Velinotamig is engineered with high-affinity binding to BCMA and lower-affinity binding to CD3, with the goal of enhancing target-cell depletion while minimizing nonspecific T cell activation and associated cytokine-related toxicity. By targeting BCMA-expressing cells, velinotamig has the potential to address autoimmune diseases driven by pathogenic autoantibodies.

Cullinan holds a global (ex-Greater China), all-indication, exclusive license to velinotamig from Genrix Bio. Genrix Bio is evaluating velinotamig in a Phase 1b/2a clinical trial in patients with refractory SLE in China (NCT07348055). Cullinan Therapeutics is also evaluating subcutaneously administered velinotamig in a global Phase 1b/2a study in patients with relapsing and refractory immune thrombocytopenia and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (NCT07738822).

Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic, heterogeneous autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks a patient’s own tissues. The most common manifestations of SLE include skin rashes, arthritis, extreme fatigue, and low fevers. Lupus nephritis (LN) is a kidney disease and the most common severe manifestation of SLE. Approximately 40% of patients with SLE develop LN, which has a 10-year 30% mortality rate.1,2 The prevalence of SLE in the US is estimated at 160,000 to 320,000 cases and SLE affects approximately 3.4 million individuals globally.3,4 SLE is more prevalent in women and people of color.5 It occurs most often in people between the ages of 15 and 45 years but can occur in childhood or later in life as well.6 Currently available treatments can reduce the signs and symptoms of SLE; however, they do not routinely induce treatment-free remission, and most patients require lifelong immune suppression that treats symptoms without modifying the course of disease.7-9

title: Velinotamig, a BCMAxCD3 T Cell Engager, Achieves Complete Renal Responses and Significantly Reduces Disease Activity in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in Data Presented at ACR Convergence 2026
